$comment: Quick-run slice of eval_full — exercises the architectural layers on the
hard regime.  All loads receive a skewed priority distribution (10 % critical /
70 % residential / 20 % curtailable) so the priority-weighted served fraction
is genuinely weighted.  Tight slack budget (constrained_30) + multi-failure
scenarios + 10 s of simulated time keep PWSF visibly < 1.
Includes two targeted holonic / CP scenarios:
- cp_flexibility_shift (generator + mixed failures): produces per-seed
cross-sector imbalance for the CP-ADMM layer to act on.
- concentrated_imbalance (failures at a single node): produces a stark
per-group deficit while adjacent groups have slack capacity, so the
Level-2 holonic ADMM is the only path to recover the lost demand.
This is the experiment specifically designed to make the holonic
layer's value visible in the metric.
name: eval_quick

$comment: CP flexibility shift: generator + mixed failures with diverse priorities.
Generator failures sometimes hit heat-side (HeatGenerator) and sometimes
power-side (PowerGenerator/CHP), producing per-seed variability in the
imbalance-vector signs.
experiments.name: cp_flexibility_shift

$comment: Concentrated imbalance — the targeted holonic-layer test.  All failures
hit branches incident to a single node, creating a local sub-community
with stark deficit while neighbouring groups retain slack capacity.
Without Level-2 holonic ADMM, the deficit group can only recover what
its intra-group gossip finds locally; with holonic ADMM, capacity is
redirected from neighbouring groups.  This is the experiment most
likely to surface a measurable scare > single_level advantage on simbench.
experiments.name: concentrated_imbalance
